title: Promotion
description: A record that a configuration was made current, or that a previous one was restored. Promotion is a label repoint, not a rebuild -- so rollback is a repoint too, and both are the same record shape with a different direction. Every field except the timestamps is a pointer: a promotion that cannot name the run justifying it is not a promotion, it is an assertion.

kind.description: rollback carries the same evidence pointers as the promotion it reverses, so the record says what was believed at the time rather than erasing it.

baseline_id.description: The baseline the candidate was measured against. Must be on the benchmark lineage; a development baseline may not certify anything.

supersedes.description: The promotion this one replaces. Written forward, on the NEW record, because evidence is immutable and the old record cannot be edited to point at its successor.

conditions.description: The five conditions, each recorded with its verdict and the reason. A promotion stores why it was allowed, not merely that it was: a conjunction whose satisfied terms are not written down degrades into a rubber stamp the first time one of them silently stops being checked.

detail.description: Why it held or did not. Required in both directions -- 'why it was allowed' is as auditable as 'why it was refused'.
